Italian, Kosher and Delicious: Chianti According to Jewish Law

The "Terra di Seta" winery, located in the heart of the Chianti region in Italy, is a kosher winery even though it doesn't have to be, and it offers a wonderful experience, excellent wines, and even a kosher dairy restaurant • Our writer visited there and returned with a wealth of experiences and recommendations

It wasn't hard to miss the narrow gravel path leading to the boutique Tuscan winery "Terra di Seta," located in the heart of the Chianti region. The paved road that had taken us from the city of Siena had ended several kilometers ago, but the GPS guided us to an unpaved road within the dark forest. Only by luck did we spot the modest sign Agriturismo Terra di Seta—directing us to an even narrower path. When we arrived, we were warmly welcomed by Daniel de la Seta, the owner of the property, which besides the winery building, also includes his private residence, three amazing and secluded accommodations, a swimming pool overlooking the horizon, a kosher dairy restaurant (open during tourist season), a vegetable garden where all the vegetables and herbs for the menu are grown, a natural forest, and of course—more than 150 acres of vineyards (almost all Sangiovese) and olive groves. The view from every direction opens the chakras—rows upon rows of vineyards in a range of green hues, and cypresses with upright bearing stretching skyward.

he: כל מפגש שלנו עם טוסקנה הוא מרגש, בייחוד כזה שבו אתה מגלה יקב נפלא וכשר. משפחת דה לה סטה היא יהודית־רומאית שורשית, ושמה מרמז על עיסוקה ההיסטורי - טוויית טליתות ממשי, שהיו נפוצות בעבר בקרב יהודי רומא. בהכשרתו דניאל הוא ביולוג ושימש מרצה בתחום באקדמיה האיטלקית. אל עבודת האדמה והיין הגיע בעקבות אשתו. "החלטנו לרכוש את השטח בתחילת המילניום ובשנים הראשונות מכרנו את הענבים ליקבי האזור", הוא מספר לנו תוך כדי שיטוט בכרמים בשעת שקיעה. "בשנת 2007 הבנו שאנחנו רוצים לעשות את היין שלנו, בנינו את היקב החדש, וכבר מההתחלה קיבלנו החלטה להכפיף את עצמנו באופן וולונטרי לשלוש מערכות רגולציה – לזו של מחוז קיאנטי קלאסיקו, לרגולציה אורגנית ולמערכת חוקי הכשרות. מכיוון שהכרמים היו זקנים ועייפים, התחלנו לשנטע (לעקור את הגפנים הוותיקות ולנטוע את הכרמים מחדש, ר"פ) את כל השטח, חלקה אחר חלקה, ורק בבציר הבא, 2022, נקלוט ענבים מהחלקה האחרונה שחודשה". איזו מערכת חוקים היא המאתגרת ביותר? דה לה סטה: "אני לא בטוח שיש תשובה לשאלה הזו. בכל מערכת חוקים יש חלקים מורכבים יותר ומורכבים פחות, וחלקם אפילו חופפים.

us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v.en: Every encounter we have with Tuscany is moving, especially one in which you discover a wonderful and kosher winery. The De La Seta family is a deeply rooted Roman-Jewish family, and its name hints at their historical occupation – the weaving of actual prayer shawls, which were once common among Roman Jews. In his training, Daniel is a biologist and served as a lecturer in the field at the Italian Academy. He came to land and wine work following his wife. "We decided to purchase the property at the beginning of the millennium and in the first years we sold the grapes to wineries in the region," he tells us while strolling through the vineyards at sunset. "In 2007 we understood that we wanted to make our own wine, we built the new winery, and from the very beginning we made the decision to voluntarily subject ourselves to three regulatory systems – that of the Chianti Classico district, organic regulation, and the system of kashrut laws. Since the vineyards were old and tired, we started to replant (uproot the old vines and replant the vineyards anew, editor's note) the entire property, plot by plot, and only in the next harvest, 2022, will we harvest grapes from the last renovated plot." Which regulatory system is the most challenging? De La Seta: "I'm not sure there is an answer to that question. In each regulatory system there are parts that are more complex and less complex, and some of them even overlap."
